title: Catalogue Token Delivery
summary: Deliver Catalogue as the first semantic-token family, with combined discovery, immutable identity, tolerant projection, and broken-link repair.
content_html:
Catalogue Token Delivery

Complete Result

Deliver Catalogue as the first complete semantic-token family:

  • combined Work, Series, and Moment discovery;
  • accepted catalogue-token syntax and family/target data contracts;
  • Add catalogue token toolbar action and required-data modal;
  • caret recognition, exact-range highlighting, Catalogue Info view, update, and removal;
  • builder parsing and manage-only usage-index generation;
  • migration of the active Work occurrence into the Catalogue family;
  • semantic-token diagnosis and repair through the existing manage-only Docs Broken Links report.

This delivery proves that an author can begin with ambiguous text, compare different catalogue entity types, choose the best association, and then maintain the occurrence without changing its identity. It does not add Tag, asset, image, file, or another token family.

This delivery is proposed and not approved for implementation.

Delivery Rule

Deliver the smallest complete vertical capability that replaces the existing Work token and leaves an additive path for later fields and token families. This delivery does not need to predict the final registry, every projection, or the next refactor.

Work, Series, and Moment share one minimal Catalogue lookup shape. The active 3 symbols Work occurrence is the migration and completion specimen. Richer type-specific fields are added only when a later UI or consumer requires them.

CT-P0 — Freeze The First Contract And Fixtures

Outcome: approve the exact source, UI, lookup, build, usage, and broken-link behavior for one resolved Work token and one broken Work token before production code changes.

  • [ ] Accept the Source Editor UI and Architecture as the direction for this slice.
  • [ ] Fix the exact Catalogue token syntax: delimiters, family, concrete target type, immutable id, Title, escaping, and deterministic serialization.
  • [ ] Fix shared Python/browser fixtures for valid, escaped, malformed, code-context, adjacent-token, and caret-boundary cases.
  • [ ] Use the existing 3 symbols Work 00638 occurrence as the resolved and migration fixture.
  • [ ] Fix one deliberately absent Work identity as the broken fixture and record its exact raw source, unchanged rendered result, and Broken Links row.
  • [ ] Retain nerve as the ambiguous discovery fixture: at minimum Work 00008 and Series 105 must be distinguishable in one result set.
  • [ ] Accept the minimum token fields: family, target type, target id, and occurrence Title.
  • [ ] Accept the minimum token-kind definition: key and labels, id policy, lookup adapter, declared lookup fields, and UI contribution ids.
  • [ ] Accept the minimum target lookup row: family/type, id, title, workable href, and optional compact meta.
  • [ ] Accept the minimum resolved usage row: source document/range, raw token, occurrence Title, target identity, and resolved href.
  • [ ] Accept the minimum semantic broken-link row: source document/range, raw token, parsed identity where available, and failure reason.
  • [ ] Name only the source-action, modal, Info-host, current-buffer, and guarded range refactors required by these fixtures.
  • [ ] Prove the fixture and JSON shapes are versioned and additive; do not build an executable config/plugin framework.

P0 may add contract fixtures and focused conformance tests. It does not change production behavior. Stop for review after P0 and do not start P1 until the fixtures and minimal shapes are accepted.

CT-P1 — Catalogue Creation UI

Outcome: an author can select or type text, search Catalogue in one modal, choose the concrete target, and insert the accepted token into the local source buffer.

  • [ ] Add one Add catalogue token source-editor toolbar action.
  • [ ] Extract the pilot title-weighted search and keyboard-navigable result list from its Info-panel host and place it in the Catalogue modal.
  • [ ] Search Work, Series, and Moment together using the shared minimal lookup row; show type, id, title, and compact meta.
  • [ ] Capture selection text and range before modal focus; use the text to seed search, prefill Title, and replace the captured range.
  • [ ] Let the author compare and change results until confirming the concrete target type and id.
  • [ ] Make modal confirmation the only semantic validation gate: require a current result, required Title, and successful serialization.
  • [ ] Add only the generic action/modal/source-adapter contribution points required by this workflow; keep Catalogue knowledge outside core.
  • [ ] Preserve local dirty state, focus return, cancellation, keyboard behavior, and the existing Rebuild ownership.

P1 review: manually review ambiguous nerve search, result distinction, selection prefilling, insertion, cancellation, keyboard use, modal fit, and narrow layout. Stop before P2 if the UI cannot express the P0 contract cleanly.

CT-P2 — Recognition, Info, And Tolerant Projection

Outcome: the inserted token can be recognized and maintained in source, and rebuild creates a link and usage relationship only when its lookup row supplies a workable destination.

  • [ ] Add the accepted token-definition registry entries for catalogue:work, catalogue:series, and catalogue:moment.
  • [ ] Generate the combined lookup with the P0 fields and accepted canonical adapters; do not expose raw canonical records or arrays.
  • [ ] Implement aligned browser and Python parsing/serialization against the P0 fixtures.
  • [ ] Detect a Catalogue token from the caret in the current unsaved buffer and select its exact source range.
  • [ ] Show a Catalogue Info view with read-only family/type/id, editable Title, declared read-only title/link context, Update token, and Remove token.
  • [ ] Keep target search and identity replacement out of the Info view; changing identity remains Remove followed by Add.
  • [ ] Guard exact-range update/removal against stale buffer offsets.
  • [ ] Resolve builder links through the target lookup rather than constructing a route from an id alone.
  • [ ] Leave malformed, unsupported, unresolved, or destination-less strings unchanged; emit no semantic link, usage row, warning, or build failure.
  • [ ] Generate by-document and by-target usage data only for resolved occurrences under the accepted semantic-tokens generated location.

P2 review: the resolved Work fixture inserts, activates, updates, removes, rebuilds to the accepted link, and appears in usage data. The broken fixture remains ordinary text and absent from usage data. Focused parser, range, registry, lookup, builder, and Info-view checks pass.

CT-P3 — Broken-Link Repair, Migration, And Cleanup

Outcome: unresolved semantic-token links have a practical repair path, the active Work token uses the new contract, and the pilot wiring is gone.

  • [ ] Extend the existing Docs Broken Links audit and report with the P0 semantic-token broken-link row; add no separate Semantic Tokens report.
  • [ ] Scan source independently of the resolved usage index and report unsupported kind, missing target, and missing workable destination.
  • [ ] Open the owning document in source mode from a report row. Select the exact occurrence only if the P0 handoff can support it without a broader editor refactor.
  • [ ] Keep repair user-controlled: fix canonical/projection data where appropriate, or Remove the source token and Add the correct target through the validated modal.
  • [ ] Migrate the active 3 symbols Work occurrence without changing its target or displayed Title.
  • [ ] Rebuild lookup and usage output rather than migrating generated JSON record by record.
  • [ ] Remove pilot names, paths, registry shape, Info-panel picker placement, route-only unresolved linking, report wiring, and public relationship copies after their replacements are active.
  • [ ] Add no compatibility aliases or public replacement.

P3 review: the broken fixture appears in Docs Broken Links with source and reason but does not block rebuild; its repair clears the audit. The migrated 3 symbols occurrence renders and indexes correctly. Focused report, route, module, and migration checks plus the targeted Docs build and git diff --check pass.

Explicitly Deferred

  • Series context on a Work occurrence;
  • preview images and other richer lookup presentation;
  • media, file, or download projections and canonical array handling;
  • occurrence fields beyond Title or a general field-control system;
  • type-specific metadata beyond the shared minimal Catalogue lookup row;
  • Tag, asset, image, file, or another token family;
  • canonical Work, Series, or Moment editing;
  • a standalone Semantic Tokens report, route, service, or validation system;
  • public semantic relationships, related-content UI, or focused public payloads;
  • automatic conversion or semantic wrapping of ordinary Markdown links or media;
  • a general plugin architecture or compatibility layer for a possible future refactor.
